chapter_seo_title: Threads of the Siming: A Dao-Twisted World Lore Bomb Reveals the Zuowandao’s True Patron
chapter_meta_description: Lü Xiucai’s encounter with Blind Chen shatters his delusions of power. Then Zhuge Yuan drops a devastating truth: the Zuowandao have a Siming too.
og_title: The Zuowandao’s Secret Patron Is Revealed
og_description: A blind man teaches Lü Xiucai the price of worthlessness, while Zhuge Yuan quietly rewrites everything you thought about the Zuowandao.
twitter_title: The Zuowandao aren’t just liars—they have a divine sponsor.
twitter_description: Lü Xiucai learns that mercy costs five copper coins, and Zhuge Yuan reveals that every falsehood runs on a higher power.

lore_anchors.definition: A terrifying, unnamed blind ascetic who uses a white banner and a bronze mirror as weapons; his power is absolute and his morality is merciless.
A local strongman killed off-screen by Blind Chen; his death serves to demonstrate the vast gap in power between thugs and true practitioners.
The grotesque, tentacled parasitic entity inside Li Huowang's carriage; here it serves as a bed for the dog and a constant reminder of bodily horror.
An Arbiter of Fate, a type of high-dimensional entity in the Dao-Twisted World. The Zuowandao also have one, making their "falsehood" a structurally equal power source.

A central philosophical dichotomy in the Dao-Twisted World, where the generic xianxia concept of "seeking truth" is literalized and opposed by the Zuowandao's power of "cultivating falsehood into reality."

cultural_notes_faq.a: A nameless blind ascetic who wields a white banner and a bronze mirror; he appears to be a rogue practitioner whose power far exceeds the local thugs.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Zhuge Yuan say he can "see threads" on the Zuowandao?
cultural_notes_faq.a: As a Heart-Embedded, Zhuge Yuan has the cognitive ability to perceive the metaphysical connection between a practitioner and their patron Siming.
A person whose soul or destiny has been occupied by a Siming, granting them supernatural cognition and making them a vessel for a higher power.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Do the Zuowandao have a Siming?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Yes—this chapter reveals that they do, which means their power to "cultivate falsehood" is backed by a genuine high-dimensional entity, not just clever tricks.
